items.editor_note: Shifts from whether scores are trustworthy to whether individual answers are, via a black-box aleatoric/epistemic split.

items.title: Jailbreak Detection on Large Language Models via Contrastive Prototype Structures
items.summary_1line: Jailbreak attempts and harmful prompts remain a challenge for the safe deployment of large language models. We study whether contrastively learned representations can support safety detection without training an addit...

editorial.tldr: This thread is a reading list of LLM research grouped by shared wording, not one event. From Oct 30 it ran through pruning, Anthropic's Nov 2 provable-inference update, knowledge editing and eval-validity work to Nov 13-16 papers on when a model should abstain, ask or escalate.
editorial.whats_new: Nov 18: a contrastive-prototype method detects jailbreak prompts without training a separate guard model, after Nov 16-17 papers on calibrated abstention thresholds and provenance-aware decoding for omnimodal hallucinations.
editorial.why_it_matters: Most items are single unreplicated preprints, but the recent run converges on guardrail design: calibrated refusal, modality-aware hallucination control and lightweight jailbreak screening, each a component a serving stack can test.
editorial.take_for_builders: Before swapping in any of these guardrails, replay your own traffic: measure the jailbreak detector's false-block rate on benign prompts, check that a calibrated abstention threshold holds its error rate on your data, and count the extra model calls each method adds.

open_questions: Does the contrastive-prototype jailbreak detector report false-positive rates on benign prompts and hold up against adaptive attacks?
Does stability-compensated threshold calibration keep its error guarantee when the deployed model or prompt distribution shifts?
Does PACD report the decoding latency or extra forward passes it adds per token?
Does TRIAGE-CPG report which models escalate too rarely or too often under a fixed analysis budget?
Do published unlearning or knowledge-editing methods still pass when probed without explicit entity names, as ShadowBench suggests they may not?
Does Anthropic publish proving cost or latency figures for zkSNARK-based provable inference?
